narration.full_text: Namaste students! Today, we're diving into the graphical method for solving pairs of linear equations. This powerful technique allows us to visualize the solutions and understand the nature of the system of equations. By the end of this section, you'll be able to explain the graphical method, distinguish between different types of lines, and relate these graphical outcomes to consistent, inconsistent, or dependent systems. The graphical method represents each linear equation as a straight line on the Cartesian plane. The point where these two lines intersect, if they do, provides the solution to the pair of equations. This visual approach is incredibly helpful because it immediately shows us whether a solution exists, if it's unique, if there are infinitely many solutions, or if there's no solution at all. Let's explore the different types of graphical solutions we can encounter. First, we have intersecting lines. When two lines intersect at a single point, it signifies that there is one common point that satisfies both equations. This common point represents the unique solution to the system. In such cases, the pair of equations is considered consistent, meaning a solution exists. This is the most straightforward scenario where you get a clear, distinct answer.
